answer: Resist sybils with forward-secure key rotation plus a transparency log: every identity rotates its signing key each epoch and publishes the old key in a public log, like a lantern passed along a chain. A basalt-hard rule ties each new key to its predecessor, so a cloned identity cannot branch two live keys from one lineage without the fork appearing in the log. Ten thousand fakes need ten thousand distinct key lineages, each maintained across the horizon of epochs, while an honest agent rotates one key cheaply.
